title: Kernel pipeline stalls and L2 contention — exploratory notes (Llama / Mistral / Qwen, MoE long-context)
body:
Purpose and scope:

Quick exploratory notes capturing an odd set of tail-latency and throughput regressions we saw on long-context MoE workloads. This is intentionally informal — observations, microbench traces, and suggested mitigations. Scope: Llama-2-13B / Mistral-7B / Qwen-Base style transformers, sequences 8k–32k, with mixed MoE layers (2-4 MoE layers, 2*exp_count). Server HW: A100 40GB and H100 80GB; OS/kernel and driver versions vary (see linked artifacts).

High-level hypothesis (working):
- We are seeing kernel pipeline stalls driven by L2 cache thrash + non-coalesced prefetch patterns when processing long-context token windows under MoE fanout.
- This interacts with our CPU->GPU DMA scheduling (PCIe/UVM lane eviction) and increases kernel launch latencies; that jitter amplifies tail latency due to serialization of small kernels between experts.

Why this is different from classic MoE fanout problems:
- Classic MoE notes focus on network fanout and expert load imbalance. Here the core symptom is higher than expected per-token kernel occupancy drop even when GPU util is nominal — measured as lower achieved occupancy during FFN/attention kernels due to L2 misses and repeated memory thrashing.

What we measured (summary):
- Setup: synthetic prompt stream and production prompts sampled; sequence lengths: 8k / 16k / 32k. Batching: single-request streaming and batch sizes 4/8 for throughput tests. MoE configuration: topk=2 gating, 64 experts per MoE block, expert hidden dim = 4096.
- Profiling tools: Nsight Systems traces, CUPTI counters, nvprof lightweight counters, internal per-kernel latency traces instrumented in runtime.

Key counters and observations:
- L2 locality degradation: L2 hit ratio drops ~8–18 percentage points with sequence length increasing from 8k->32k for Qwen and Mistral. Llama shows a smaller drop (~4–6%).
- DRAM bandwidth: sustained bandwidth increases (expected) but with larger variance; peak bursts coincide with gate routing windows.
- Kernel launch latency: median small-kernel launch ~20–40 us, but 95/99 spikes up to 150–250 us aligned with peaks in L2 miss bursts.
- CU occupancy: average CU occupancy during attention and FFN fused kernels drops 10–20% during stress windows despite overall GPU utilization still being ~70–85% measured over long intervals.
- UVM/pagefault-like behavior: on A100s with UVM enabled for certain tests, we saw sporadic device page fault handling events correlated with long-context boundary crossings (rare but high-cost events).

Per-model differences (observed):
- Qwen-Base: worst L2 hit-rate deterioration. Likely due to larger key/value projection sizes and different memory layout produced by our compilation path. Kernel launch jitter and page-tiling offsets appear to matter more.
- Mistral-7B: intermediate; fused attention kernel appears to tolerate tiling shifts better, so stalls are somewhat less extreme but still present.
- Llama-2-13B: least impacted; per-layer memory working set smaller per token in our implementation (tile-friendly) and our quantization path produced more contiguous memory accesses.

MoE-specific interactions:
- Expert fanout creates many short-lived kernels (small FFN per-expert calls) — these are sensitive to kernel launch jitter and L2 priming.
- When many tokens route to the same few experts (hot experts), L2 and per-SM cache lines are repeatedly re-used (good) but when routing is more uniform the random access pattern across experts causes cacheline churn and increases misses.
- KV cache prefetch/eviction interplay: long-context sessions cause large KV caches; evictions sometimes align with expert-switch windows, amplifying miss rates.

Concrete evidence from traces (selected):
- Nsight system timeline: repeated sequence of small kernel launches separated by 30–80 us normally, but at 95/99 percentiles we see sequences with 150–230 us gaps. These align with L2-cache-miss spikes from CUPTI.
- Hotspot: the first FFN micro-kernel after a token routing change has ~3x higher DRAM reads than steady-state subsequent micro-kernels — suggests prefetching/warmup behavior missing.
- Memory profiling: stride distribution of loads shows increased non-unit stride accesses in Qwen pathways; codegen tiling emits gather-like patterns for some projection shapes.

Quick experiments we ran (ad-hoc):
1) Kernel coalescing: coalesced small per-expert kernels into larger fused launches (packing multiple experts into a single kernel invocation) — result: 20–35% tail-latency improvement and smoothing of L2 miss spikes for Qwen/Mistral. Tradeoff: temporary increase in per-kernel memory working set.
2) Artificial pre-warm: intentionally run a tiny priming kernel that touches the relevant KV/FFN pages for an upcoming expert batch — reduced first-kernel spike but added cost overall; net win for tail latency in interactive setting.
3) Tiling changes: switch to an alternative memory layout (column-major vs row-major variant for projection matrices) — improved L2 hit-rate on Qwen traces but required new kernel code paths.
4) PCIe transfer batching: combined small DMA transfers into chunked transfers to reduce interrupt/context churn — reduced jitter marginally on A100 tests.

Actionable mitigations (rank-ordered, pragmatic):
- Short-term (low-risk):
  - Aggregate small per-expert kernels when possible (runtime packing) for long-context and MoE-heavy requests. Enable as heuristic when sequence_length>8k or when per-request expert-count>32.
  - Add a configurable lightweight prefetch/priming kernel to warm L2 for upcoming expert sets (enable for tail-latency-sensitive endpoints only).
  - Instrument and alert on L2 miss-rate and kernel launch latency per model route (console dashboard).
- Medium-term:
  - Implement a compile-time codegen path for Qwen that prefers unit-stride loads for projection kernels (investigate GEMM/tensorization tweaks producing contiguous reads).
  - Explore fused expert dispatch kernels that perform gating+dispatch+FFN in one kernel to cut launch overhead and reduce intermediate memory churn.
- Long-term / research:
  - Adaptive locality-aware routing: modify gating to prefer experts that improve memory locality (soft penalty for switching experts that incur new page/tiling hitters). This may reduce model-perplexity initially — needs eval tradeoffs.
  - Kernel-level L2-friendly prefetching heuristics inside the fused kernels themselves (prefetch UVM pages, pre-touch).

Open questions / unknowns:
- Is there a compiler/runtime interaction unique to the Qwen model build that we can reproduce in microbench? Need a minimal repro showing gather-like access pattern.
- How much of the jitter is caused by host-side scheduling vs GPU-side cache effects? (Runs with NVTX timeline + host perf counters to correlate.)
- What is the cost/perf impact of packing kernels in high-QPS multi-tenant situations? Does packing harm overall throughput under saturated GPU because of larger working set footprints?

Next steps (owner: Ava, supported by Liam/Marisol):
- Create a small synthetic microbenchmark that reproduces Qwen projection stride pattern and run tiled L2 counter sweeps (target due: 2025-02-20).
- Implement a runtime flag to pack per-expert kernels and run A/B on production traffic (canary on dedicated cluster) — collect 50/95/99 latency histograms (target due: 2025-03-03).
- Add a dashboard panel for per-model L2 miss-rate and kernel-launch-latency (owner: Marisol) — link to alerting thresholds (target due: 2025-02-27).

Notes to self / friction points:
- Be careful with UVM tests; page-fault behavior depends heavily on driver/kernel combos, might be noisy. Re-run on same OS/kernel when reproducing.
- When packing kernels, ensure we preserve semantic ordering for model outputs (serial vs parallel execution tradeoffs).

References and snippets:
- See PR 1876: prototype packing and priming kernels (linked artifact).
- Example nvprof counters of interest to capture: l2_subp0_read_transactions, l2_subp0_write_transactions, dram_read_bytes, sm_efficiency, inst_executed

Bottom line (current):
We have a credible signal that long-context MoE workloads for some model builds (notably Qwen) suffer from L2 cache locality and kernel-launch jitter that together drive tail latency. Practical wins exist by packing small kernels and adding targeted priming; medium-term wins require codegen/layout fixes and maybe gating changes. This is high-priority for any interactive endpoint with >8k context and MoE layers.

TODO / backlog (short list):
- Minimal repro + run on both A100 and H100 and report differences (owner: Liam).
- Evaluate semantic impact of locality-biased gating in offline evals (owner: research).
- Measure multi-tenant packing impact under high sustained throughput (owner: infra/perf).

End of notes.
